newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan, not China, seen as Taiwan's No.1 foe.
newsitem.headline: Japan, not China, seen as Taiwan's No.1 foe.

text.p: Stirred to fury by a dispute over the uninhabited Diaoyu Islands, Taiwanese militants caused chaos at the check-out of a Japanese department store on Sunday while a ganster-backed "suicide squad" vowed to raid the islands and blow up a Japanese-built lighthouse.
While the government continues to fight a cold war with Peking, so far as Taiwan's people are concerned Japan has displaced China as Public Enemy Number One.

"The Japanese are invading our territory, so why are we still buying Japanese products?" said a member of the "Association for the Protection of Diaoyu Islands", which held a rally in the basement of Taipei's popular Japanese-owned SOGO Department Store on Sunday.

As part of the protest, over 100 members of the association filled shopping carts with Japan-made products at SOGO's supermarket, they refused to buy them after cashiers had totalled up the prices, creating long queues.
The protesters waved banners that read "Let's refuse together to buy Japanese".

A dispute over the Diaoyus, called the Senkakus in Japanese and located in East China Sea, erupted in July after the right-wing Japan Youth Federation erected a lighthouse there, angering rival claimants Taiwan and China.
The Taiwanese became outraged in recent days after Tokyo, effectively supporting the rightists, sent patrol ships to repel private Taiwan vessels that tried to approach the islands.

Tokyo's aggression has shifted Taiwan's attention away from its ongoing row with Beijing, which in the past two years has drawn Taiwan people's ire by launching intimidatory war games near the island.
Just as China's sabre-rattling angered the Taiwanese by threatening their sovereignty, Japan now is touching on the same nerve.
Many have criticised their government for taking too conciliatory a stance in the Diaoyu dispute, and some even suggested that Taipei enlist the help of the other Chinese government -- Beijing.
Taipei and Beijing separated after a bitter civil war in 1949 resulted in a defeated Republic of China government taking refuge in Taiwan in 1949.
Tired of government inaction, a group of paroled criminals backed by gangsters said on Saturday that they would embark on a "dare-to-die" mission to bomb Japan's Diaoyu lighthouse.

"We are launching the mission out of love for our country, so I hope the government does not interfere," said Tung Nie-tai, head of a private prisoners' rehabilitation centre to which the criminals belong.

The government, meanwhile, has continued to appeal for calm and vows to resolve the dispute through negotiations with Japan. But Japan, which does not have diplomatic ties with Taiwan, has not responded to Taipei's call for talks.
Private groups are creating their own channels to voice displeasure.
Members of the opposition New Party staged a rally on Sunday in the southern Kaohsiung city to gather protesting signatures.
The "Republic of China Patriot Organisation" plans to hold a 72-hour sit-in protest in front of Japan's visa office -- already the site of a rally last week -- from Monday to Wednesday.
The Association for Protection of Diaoyu Islands said in a statement it would try to tie up the visa office's phone lines on Tuesday, and then "occupy" the office on Wednesday.
It did not elaborate on how it plans to accomplish either.
